title: Invariants of an outage schedule

blocks.text: A grid operator (fictional) generates planned-outage schedules for testing its maintenance scheduler: thousands of schedules from different seeds. Before any of them reaches the scheduler, each is checked against the rules every schedule must keep. An outage takes a site out of service for `weeks` consecutive weeks from `start_week`, and needs `crew` crews in each of those weeks.

Write `violations(outages, crews_per_week)` in `outages.py`. It returns a list of strings, one per broken rule, each starting with the rule's name and a colon; a schedule that keeps every rule gives an empty list. The rules and the lines they produce:

rows: an id is used by more than one outage
`unique ids: O1`, once per such id
an outage lasts no week, starts before week 1, or runs past week 52
two outages at one site are out in a common week
`one outage per site: O1 and O2`, smaller id first
the outages active in a week need more than `crews_per_week` crews

blocks.text: `active_weeks(o)` gives the weeks an outage is out. The lines come in the table's order: the `unique ids` lines first (ids sorted), then the `inside the year` lines in the order the outages are listed, then the `one outage per site` lines (by the list position of the pair's smaller-id outage, then of the other), then the `crews suffice` lines by week, earliest first. Ids are compared as strings, so "smaller id first" puts `O10` before `O2`; two outages sharing one id are left to the unique-ids rule. The crews rule counts every week an outage is active, including the weeks past 52 of an outage that also breaks "inside the year".
The tests check the rule names, the full line for the crews rule and for duplicate ids, and the full list for one schedule that breaks every rule. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from outages import Outage, violations

sound = [Outage("U1", "Birch", 20, 2, 1), Outage("U2", "Birch", 22, 3, 2), Outage("U3", "Cedar", 21, 2, 2)]
print("three outages, 3 crews a week:", violations(sound, crews_per_week=3))

broken = [Outage("U1", "Birch", 20, 4, 2), Outage("U2", "Birch", 22, 1, 1),
          Outage("U2", "Cedar", 50, 4, 1)]
for line in violations(broken, crews_per_week=2):
    print("broken plan, 2 crews a week:", line)

cases.says: a sound schedule gives no violations, and a broken one names each rule it breaks
an outage whose last week is week 52 is inside the year, and one running into week 53 is not
two outages at one site, one starting the week after the other ends, do not overlap
an outage's crews count in every week it lasts, not only its first
an id used three times is reported once
the lines come rule by rule in the stated order, and O10 is the smaller id of O10 and O2
an outage running past week 52 still needs its crews in weeks 53 and on
